findings.title: Migration crashes when 'embed_category' site_setting was never customized
findings.body: The migration does `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Site settings are normally only persisted in the `site_settings` table when an admin has explicitly changed them from their default value. Since `embed_category` defaulted to `''`, the vast majority of installations will have no row with `name = 'embed_category'`, so the query returns zero rows and `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`. Calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration for essentially every typical install (and for test/CI databases that never touched this setting). The fallback for `category_id == 0` is never reached because the exception happens before it.

findings.title: Unescaped string interpolation in raw SQL INSERT
findings.body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` interpolates the `host` value (pulled from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which could contain arbitrary characters such as single quotes) directly into the SQL string without using `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` or parameter binding. A host value containing a single quote will break the INSERT (syntax error, migration failure) or corrupt the migration's intent; this is a data-integrity risk in the migration path.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `before_validation { self.host.sub!(...); self.host.sub!(...) }` assumes `host` is always a String. If `host` is nil (e.g. the admin submits the form with no host value, or `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing as set in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`), `self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of surfacing a normal `validates_format_of`/presence validation error. This turns a user input mistake into an unhandled 500 error.

findings.title: update/destroy do not handle a missing EmbeddableHost record
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` when no matching record exists. In `update`, the subsequent `save_host(host)` call will do `host.host = ...` on `nil`, raising `NoMethodError`. In `destroy` (line 15-16), `host.destroy` is called directly on a possibly-nil object, also raising `NoMethodError`. Neither action returns a proper 404/error response for an invalid id; both will surface as unhandled 500 errors instead.

findings.title: Fabricator file content doesn't match its filename (content appears swapped)
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now only defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly-added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `Fabricator(:category)`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category`. The contents of the two files appear to have been swapped: the category fabricators ended up in the file named for embeddable hosts, and vice versa. Fabrication doesn't care about filenames so tests still pass, but this is confusing and will mislead future maintainers looking for category or embeddable-host fabricators by filename.

findings.title: New controller spec only checks class inheritance, not actual behavior
findings.body: The spec for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`. None of the new `create`, `update`, or `destroy` actions (including the error paths discussed above, such as missing-id handling or invalid host validation) are exercised, leaving the new admin endpoints for managing embeddable hosts essentially untested.

findings.title: New controller spec only checks class inheritance, not actual behavior
findings.body: Similar to the embeddable_hosts controller spec, this spec for `Admin::EmbeddingController` only checks that it is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. The `show`/`update` actions and the `fetch_embedding` before_filter are not tested at all, so regressions in the embedding admin endpoint would not be caught.
